title: Human rights & international treaties (educational summary)
articleRef: Political Constitution of the United Mexican States (overview)
excerpt: Educational summary: constitutional reforms have elevated human-rights standards, requiring authorities to apply international human rights treaties as the ‘parameter of interpretation’ alongside constitutional guarantees—implementation details still turn on courts and statutes.

title: Federal model — states & federation (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: Mexico is a federal republic; powers are divided among federal, state, and municipal levels. Civil and criminal law can vary by state in permitted domains, while federal authorities handle enumerated federal matters.

title: Individual guarantees — amparo tradition (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the Constitution protects individual guarantees (liberty, hearing, privacy, expression, etc.). The juicio de amparo is a historic remedy against laws or acts violating guarantees, subject to procedural rules and jurisprudence.

title: Congress & legislative power (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the Congress of the Union exercises federal legislative power through bicameral processes (with exceptions for certain resolutions). Checks between chambers and the executive shape how bills become law.
